newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian shares down under Israeli closure.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian shares down under Israeli closure.

text.p: Palestinian shares closed lower on Wednesday in very weak trading as the West Bank and Gaza remained under an Israeli security closure, the Palestinian Securities Exchange (PSE) said.
The Jerusalem Index dropped 0.4 percent to 104.65 on low turnover of 31,290 shares valued at 53,090 Jordanian dinars, compared with Sunday's all time low 4,431 shares worth 14,953 dinars.
The exchange holds two sessions a week.
"This is abnormally low," said PSE General Manager Safwan Batayneh. "We should expect very slow trading and weak prices for the duration of the closure."

Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza after two suicide bombers killed 14 people in a Jewish market on July 30. Israel says it will ease its siege when the Palestinian Authority cracks down on militants.

"Although the exchange is operating normally with traders entering orders from offices throughout the West Bank, trades originate with customers and people are dealing with securities as the end of their priorities list," Batayneh said.
Shares in Palestine Telecommunication Co, the most active stock, closed unchanged at 1.55 dinars.
The Arab Co. for Paint Products rose 1.48 percent to 1.37 dinars and Palestine Real Estate Investment Co. dropped two percent to 0.98 dinars.
Trading is conducted in dollars or dinars in the absence of a Palestinian currency. The exchange first began publishing an index on July 13.
